b09dfad591.q: What workflow does Spectora's AI use to match voice recordings to inspection comments?
b09dfad591.a: Inspectors take photos grouped into collections, then record audio describing defects and information for that collection. The AI processes the audio and fetches matching comments from the inspector's report template. During review, the system presents one comment at a time for the inspector to approve and add photos, maintaining the inspector's words and template rather than generating new content.

b2399b928e.q: Why does Spectora embed AI directly into report writing instead of generic integration?
b2399b928e.a: Megan explained that Spectora looked at specific problems in the product first, viewing AI as a tool to solve pain points rather than adding it just for marketing. The main problem identified was inspectors spending excessive time on data entry, searching through the app, and scrolling to find the right comments instead of focusing on their core expertise of inspecting and identifying defects.

03776a4b98.q: How does Spectora's AI approach address inspector concerns about AI replacement?
03776a4b98.a: Spectora matches AI-suggested comments directly to the inspector's existing template and comments rather than generating new text, keeping the inspector's voice and expertise central. Megan stated the goal is to empower inspectors to do more with their time and focus on their expertise, never to replace them, since home inspection requires deep knowledge of electrical, plumbing, and multiple other systems that AI cannot autonomously handle on site.
